newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks firm, volume led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks firm, volume led by blue chips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks were steady in early trade on Monday as profit-taking fizzled out and volumes were supported by activity in two blue chips, brokers said.
The all share index was 0.32 points higher, at 607.22, at the mid-morning break.
"The index is firm because profit-taking which brought prices down, has run out," said Ajit Dias Wanigasekera a trader at Commercial Stock Brokers.
But the index would be ranged as retail investors, who usually move prices, have other spending priorities due to the on-coming December holiday season, he said.
Early turnover was at 51.6 million rupees, on trading of blue chips John Keells Holdings Ltd and Ceylon Grain Elevators Ltd.
A parcel of 240,000 shares of John Keells Holdings traded 25 cents up at 192, and a total of 270,000 Grain Elevators traded 75 cents up at 1.25.
